title: Issue-tracker API key returned in product API responses to any user with read (View) permission
rationale: Root cause is `ProductCoreSerializer.to_representation` at backend/application/core/api/serializers_product.py:123. It serializes every model field (the base `Meta.fields = "__all__"`, inherited via `__all__`/`exclude` by the subclasses) and never masks `issue_tracker_api_key`. The fix pops `issue_tracker_api_key` from the output unless the caller holds `Permissions.Product_Edit`, reusing the `permissions` value the serializer already computes via `get_permissions`. It mirrors the existing precedent `ApiConfigurationSerializer.to_representation` (import_observations/api/serializers.py:111-119) that gates `api_key` on `Api_Configuration_Edit`. Placing it in the base `to_representation` fixes both serializers named in the finding (`ProductSerializer` and `ProductListSerializer`) at one inheritance point. The field stays writable (no `write_only`), so `validate()` at line 377 — which reads `attrs.get("issue_tracker_api_key")` from input — is unaffected; this only filters the *response* representation. `data.pop(..., None)` is null-safe for serializers that exclude the field.
variants_checked: ProductCoreSerializer.to_representation (base, the fix site), ProductSerializer.Meta, ProductListSerializer.Meta — all three resolve to the single inherited `to_representation`. Also grepped every `issue_tracker_api_key` usage: core/models.py:101 (field def), serializers_product.py:385/390 (input validation, unaffected), and the three issue_tracker backends (gitlab/github/jira_issue_tracker.py) which read the field server-side, not via the API serializer. NestedProductSerializer/NestedProductListSerializer/NestedProductSerializerSmall do NOT inherit ProductCoreSerializer (they subclass ModelSerializer directly): the small/list nested ones use `fields`/`exclude` that omit issue tracker fields anyway; NestedProductSerializer (excludes only members/auth groups) is used as `product_data` inside ApiConfigurationSerializer/ProductMemberSerializer — these expose the product's full field set including the key, so they would need the same gate. Flagged below rather than silently expanding scope, since the finding scopes f001 to ProductSerializer/ProductListSerializer and NestedProductSerializer is a separate sink with its own permission context.
bypass_considered: I tried reaching the key through the list endpoint (`ProductListSerializer`) since the finding flags it separately — but it inherits the same base `to_representation`, so the pop applies there too. I also considered a Reader spoofing the gate: the check reads `data["permissions"]`, which is produced server-side by `get_permissions(get_highest_user_role(obj))` from the requesting user's actual role, not from client input, so a Reader cannot inject `Product_Edit`. The one genuine residual path is `NestedProductSerializer` (e.g. embedded as `product_data` in API-configuration/member responses), which does not inherit this base and still emits the key — that is a distinct sink outside f001's stated scope and is called out in variants_checked for a follow-up finding rather than masked here, since over-broadening would change unrelated serializer contracts.
test_note: Added `test_issue_tracker_api_key_hidden_without_edit` to backend/unittests/core/api/test_serializers.py in the existing `TestBranchSerializer` class (same class the sibling `test_get_permissions_user` lives in), following the established `@patch(... get_permissions_for_role / get_highest_user_role)` pattern. It asserts the key is absent for a Reader (Product_View only) and present for Product_Edit. Fails before the change (key always serialized), passes after.
review_reason: The fix lands in `ProductCoreSerializer.to_representation` (diff line 7-10), the base-class method inherited by `ProductSerializer` at source line 272/295, so it is squarely on the call path from the LOCATION; `issue_tracker_api_key` (a credential CharField, models.py:101) is otherwise serialized to any View-permission user because line 295's exclude list omits it. It is a root-cause authorization gate keyed on the already-computed `Permissions.Product_Edit`, fails closed via `data.get("permissions") or []`, adds no new input parsing or weakened validation, and the only other inheritor (`ProductGroupSerializer`) excludes the field so the `pop(..., None)` is a safe no-op. The accompanying test hunk covers both the hidden and visible cases, and the change matches surrounding serializer style.
